notebook: First run of a region: everything is unknown. Catch early, heal before gyms, and write down EVERY gym leader's types and levels.
Kanto Gym 1 (Brock): Rock/Ground types. Psyduck's Water Bubble 4x effective. Lead Water type and it's an easy sweep.
Kanto Gym 2 (Misty): Water types. Ivysaur with Energy Ball (90 Grass STAB, 4x on Water) one-shots her whole team at Lv22. Easiest sweep if you have strong Grass.

Kanto Map 2 Scientist (Electric/Poison) at Lv5 is dangerous - it fainted my Lv15 Kadabra and Lv22 Psyduck. Trainers with type advantage can one-shot. Always check if your lead has enough bulk to survive a hit before a trainer fight, not just if you can KO back.
Map 3 Kanto Firebreather (Fire types): even with Psyduck's Water Bubble 4x, took damage that fainted Psyduck. Firebreathers hit hard. Heal Psyduck or swap to tankier lead next time.

Kanto Map 3 has TWO Firebreather trainers (layers 2 and 3). They fainted 4/6 of my team even with type advantage. If you see a second Firebreather, consider healing between or avoiding one. They hit HARD.
Start of run: pick character (no gameplay impact), then choose starter. Always check map layers before choosing - use what_lies_ahead.

Kanto starter: Squirtle (Water 4x vs Rock/Ground, resists Rock) safest for Brock. Bulbasaur's Grass is ALSO 4x vs Rock/Ground but takes 2x from Rock moves. Charmander's Fire is 0.5x - worst pick. Squirtle is the safe pick for Kanto map 0.
Kanto Map 0: safe path is catch→item→wild→move tutor→item(pokecenter layer 7). Bulbasaur with Expert Belt+Solar Beam one-shots Brock. Heal before gym always.
Kanto Map 0: n3_0 (item) leads to trainer on n4_0 (n4_1 also trainer). The two catch nodes (n5_0, n5_1) are reachable from both. Plan: item→trainers for levels→catches→pokecenter→gym.

Kanto starter analysis: Squirtle (Water 4x vs Rock/Ground) safest for Brock. Bulbasaur's Grass is ALSO 4x vs Rock/Ground (not 0.25x), but Bulbasaur is Poison type which is weak to Ground moves. Charmander's Fire is 0.5x - worst pick. Squirtle is the safe choice.

Kanto Map 1: item (n2_1) leads to catch+trainer on layer 3; n4_1 (catch) leads to trade+trainer on layer 5, then trainer+pokecenter on layer 7 before Misty. Route pattern: item→trainer→catch→trainer→?→trainer→pokecenter→gym.

Kanto Map 0 Bug Catcher trainer: even at Lv8, Squirtle fainted to it. Bug moves (like Fury Cutter) are neutral to Water but still deal decent damage. Arrive at Lv10+ for safety, or heal between fights.

Kanto Map 1: Tangela (Grass) caught layer 1 is Misty counter. Magical Leaf 40 Grass STAB + Expert Belt (+100% SE) = 480 effective vs Water. Level to Lv15+ for safe sweep. Shell Bell or Expert Belt both work well on Tangela.
Kanto Map 0 layer 5 wild battle nearly wiped my Lv6-8 team (Squirtle, Exeggcute fainted). Wild battles hit harder than expected at low levels. Heal at pokecenter before gym is mandatory.
Kanto Map 1 Misty (Water gym): all-Water team is useless (Water resists Water). Need Grass (4x) or Electric (2x) type. Catch early on this map for a counter.

Kanto Map 1 Scientist (Electric/Poison) hits HARD - wiped 5/6 of my Lv10-14 team even with Rhyhorn's Ground Bulldoze 2x. The Scientist has TWO Pokemon and both hit hard. Arrive with Lv14+ Ground type OR heal between. This trainer is a run-ender if you're underlevelled.
Kanto Map 1: pokecenter is at layer 7 (n7_1) before Misty gym at layer 8. Always heal Bellsprout there - Grass 4x vs Water is the Misty counter.
Kanto Map 1 layer 7: the ? node is an ITEM, not a catch. If you need a type counter for Misty, don't gamble on ? - take the pokecenter and hope you caught Grass/Electric earlier.
Map 5 Fisherman (Water types) fainted 4/6 of my Lv37-47 team. Water trainers hit HARD even with Grass leads. Heal BEFORE Fisherman, not after - or skip it if team is fragile.
Parasect's Megahorn is BUG type, not Grass. Bug is neutral vs Water (0.5x). Don't lead Parasect vs Water thinking Megahorn is SE - check the move's type, not the Pokemon's type.
Kanto Map 1 layer 3 ? node is a BATTLE, not an item. It fainted my Lv13 Wartortle and Lv12 Bellsprout. Avoid it if your Misty counters are fragile - take the trade instead.

Fire is 2x SUPER EFFECTIVE vs Grass, not resisted. I lost Exeggcute leading it vs Officer (Fire). Grass resists Electric (0.5x) and Water (0.5x), but takes 2x from Fire, Ice, Poison, Flying, Bug. Memorize the type chart, don't guess.

Kanto Map 2 gym is Lt. Surge (Electric). Need Ground type (immune to Electric, 2x SE). Graveler/Geodude line is perfect - Rock/Ground resists Normal and Flying too. Catch Ground type early on this map.

Kanto Map 3 gym is Erika (Grass). Fire type (Charmeleon/Charizard) with Flamethrower 2x vs Grass is the perfect counter. Graveler/Rock types take 4x from Grass - keep in back. Catch Fire type early on this map.

Metronome item: dual-type holder uses its OTHER type for attacks. Ivysaur (Grass/Poison) with Metronome uses Poison type - 2x SE vs Grass. Check dual-type Pokemon for hidden type advantages with this item.
Kanto Map 5 (after Koga): next gym is Sabrina (Psychic). Need Dark/Ghost/Bug type. Magnezone (Steel 0.5x) best defensive option. Catch early on this map for a Psychic counter.

Kanto Map 5 Hiker (Rock/Ground, Lv40+) fainted my Magnezone AND Flareon despite Steel immunity to Ground. These trainers hit EXTREMELY hard - expect casualties even with type advantage. Heal fragile Pokemon before Hiker.
Kanto Map 0: catch on layer 1 (n1_0) gives a second body early. With only Squirtle, one bad crit ends the run. Always catch early on map 0.
notes.plan: Kanto Map 3 (Erika Grass gym): Nidorino (Poison 2x vs Grass, resists Grass 0.5x) is the Erika counter. Route: catch on layer 1 (n1_0) for a 6th Pokemon body, then trainer layers for XP. Need to find a Fire type if possible for future maps. Heal at pokecenter (layer 7) before Erika gym (layer 8).

Kanto Gym 1 (Brock): Rock/Ground types. Psyduck's Water Bubble 4x effective. Lead Water type and it's an easy sweep.
Kanto Gym 2 (Misty): Water types. Ivysaur with Energy Ball (90 Grass STAB, 4x on Water) one-shots her whole team at Lv22. Easiest sweep if you have strong Grass.

Kanto Map 2 Scientist (Electric/Poison) at Lv5 is dangerous - it fainted my Lv15 Kadabra and Lv22 Psyduck. Trainers with type advantage can one-shot. Always check if your lead has enough bulk to survive a hit before a trainer fight, not just if you can KO back.
Map 3 Kanto Firebreather (Fire types): even with Psyduck's Water Bubble 4x, took damage that fainted Psyduck. Firebreathers hit hard. Heal Psyduck or swap to tankier lead next time.

Kanto Map 3 has TWO Firebreather trainers (layers 2 and 3). They fainted 4/6 of my team even with type advantage. If you see a second Firebreather, consider healing between or avoiding one. They hit HARD.
Start of run: pick character (no gameplay impact), then choose starter. Always check map layers before choosing - use what_lies_ahead.
Kanto starter: Squirtle (Water Bubble/Surf 4x) beats Brock easily. Bulbasaur's Grass is 0.25x vs Rock/Ground - WORST for Brock. Charmander's Fire is 0.5x. Squirtle is the safe pick for Kanto map 0.
Kanto Map 0: safe path is catch→item→wild→move tutor→item(pokecenter layer 7). Bulbasaur with Expert Belt+Solar Beam one-shots Brock. Heal before gym always.
Kanto Map 0: n3_0 (item) leads to trainer on n4_0 (n4_1 also trainer). The two catch nodes (n5_0, n5_1) are reachable from both. Plan: item→trainers for levels→catches→pokecenter→gym.
Kanto starter: Squirtle beats Brock (Rock/Ground) 4x with Bubble. Bulbasaur's Grass is 0.25x vs Rock/Ground, NOT 4x. Revise note [8] next chance.

Kanto Map 1: item (n2_1) leads to catch+trainer on layer 3; n4_1 (catch) leads to trade+trainer on layer 5, then trainer+pokecenter on layer 7 before Misty. Route pattern: item→trainer→catch→trainer→?→trainer→pokecenter→gym.

Kanto Map 0 Bug Catcher trainer: even at Lv8, Squirtle fainted to it. Bug moves (like Fury Cutter) are neutral to Water but still deal decent damage. Arrive at Lv10+ for safety, or heal between fights.
Kanto Map 1: caught Tangela (Grass) on layer 1 - perfect counter for Misty's Water gym. Grass 4x vs Water. Level Tangela to Lv14+ before Misty for safe sweep.
Kanto Map 0 layer 5 wild battle nearly wiped my Lv6-8 team (Squirtle, Exeggcute fainted). Wild battles hit harder than expected at low levels. Heal at pokecenter before gym is mandatory.
Kanto Map 1 Misty (Water gym): all-Water team is useless (Water resists Water). Need Grass (4x) or Electric (2x) type. Catch early on this map for a counter.

Kanto Map 1 Scientist (Electric/Poison): lead Ground type (Diglett/Rhyhorn with Bulldoze 2x) NOT Water. BUT the Scientist hits HARD - Rhyhorn Lv8 got one-shot even with type advantage. Arrive with Lv12+ Ground type or heal between. Two Pokemon per trainer on map 1.
Kanto Map 1: pokecenter is at layer 7 (n7_1) before Misty gym at layer 8. Always heal Bellsprout there - Grass 4x vs Water is the Misty counter.
Kanto Map 1 layer 7: the ? node is an ITEM, not a catch. If you need a type counter for Misty, don't gamble on ? - take the pokecenter and hope you caught Grass/Electric earlier.
Map 5 Fisherman (Water types) fainted 4/6 of my Lv37-47 team. Water trainers hit HARD even with Grass leads. Heal BEFORE Fisherman, not after - or skip it if team is fragile.
Parasect's Megahorn is BUG type, not Grass. Bug is neutral vs Water (0.5x). Don't lead Parasect vs Water thinking Megahorn is SE - check the move's type, not the Pokemon's type.
runs.plan: Kanto Map 1: caught Tangela (Grass) on layer 2 - perfect Misty counter. Now level Tangela through wild/trainer battles on layers 3-6, then heal at pokecenter on layer 7, then sweep Misty's Water gym on layer 8. Tangela needs Lv14+ for safe sweep.
